references.text: The parallel account in Mark describes the same possessed man who lived among the tombs and whom no one could bind, not even with chains. He tore apart chains and shackles and dwelt in the wilderness – exactly the same details as in Luke 8:29.
Matthew's parallel account about the demon-possessed men in the region of the Gerasenes, where Jesus commands the unclean spirits to come out.
Jesus commands an unclean spirit to leave a man, demonstrating his authority over unclean spirits – the same pattern seen in Luke 8:29 where he commanded the unclean spirit to come out.
Jesus drives out an unclean spirit in the synagogue at Capernaum, showing the same authority to command unclean spirits as we see in Luke 8:29.
Jesus' teaching about the unclean spirit that leaves a person and wanders through dry places – a thematic link to the unclean spirit that drove the man out into the wilderness.
After the possessed man was healed, he sat clothed and in his right mind – contrasting with the condition described in Luke 8:29 where he was driven by demons into the wilderness.
The man with the evil spirit overpowered them with great strength, reminiscent of the supernatural power of the demon-possessed man in Luke 8:29 who broke chains and shackles.
Description of people living among tombs and spending the night in hidden places – a thematic parallel to the possessed man who lived among the tombs and in the wilderness.
